contexts.text: In the supreme sense, it = the Lord Himself. AC 2187:3.

In the supreme sense, it = the Divine marriage.
The internal sense concerning the Lord is the supreme sense.
The internal sense is representative of the supreme sense.
The Divine Itself is in the supreme sense of the Word, because the Lord is there...
The Word as to the supreme sense is the Lord Himself...
In the supreme sense it treats of how the Lord made the Human with Himself Divine... AC 3939:end. AC 3993:3. AC 4402.
In so far as the Lord is the Word, it may be said that... the supreme sense is represented by Abraham.

In the supreme sense, it = the Divine love.
In the supreme sense, it = Foresight.
The supreme sense, which treats of the Lord, is such that it appears divided in the sense of the letter, but it is one in the supreme internal sense.
In the supreme sense, it = conjunction through good and truth in the Lord's Natural.

The supreme sense of the Word, in which the Lord is treated of, is for the Third Heaven... Man is such that the interior, and also the internal, and the supreme sense, can be communicated to him; for man communicates with the three Heavens...
In the supreme sense, in which the Lord is treated of...
As the things in the supreme sense are concerning the Lord, and surpass the ideas of man's thought, for they are Divine, (we may illustrate this by the regeneration of man). AC 6716:4. AC 6827.
For that which is represented, in the supreme sense, relates to Him.
In the supreme sense, it = the Divine good of the Divine love for saving the human race.
The Word contains heavenly things, and, in the supreme sense, Divine ones.
In the inmost and supreme sense, there is the Divine marriage which is in the Lord, thus the Lord Himself.

In the whole Word, in its inmost or supreme sense, it treats of the Lord alone, and of the glorification of His Human; but, as the inmost or supreme sense transcends the human understanding, we may explain the Word as to its internal sense...
Therefore the things which are understood of the Lord in the supreme sense, are understood of the faithful in the relative internal sense.
In the supreme sense, by the passover is represented the damnation of the unfaithful, and the deliverance of the faithful by the Lord, when He had been glorified...
In the supreme sense it treats of the Lord Himself; in which sense also there is the veriest Divine truth.
In the supreme sense, where Divine good and truth Divine are treated of, there is consociation as to a Divine celestial state.
In the supreme sense, where it treats of the Lord, there are Foresight and Providence.
Therefore in the supreme sense of the Word, it treats of the Lord alone, of His love. Providence, His Kingdom in the Heavens and on earth, and especially of the glorification of His Human. AC 9503:2.
A ram = the good of innocence and charity in the internal man; and, in the supreme sense, the same in the internal of the Lord's Human.
For all things which in the internal sense = such things as are of the Church and Heaven, in the supreme sense = Divine things.
In the supreme sense of the Word there is the Lord Himself...
